key_insight: ParetoSlider post-trains diffusion models to learn a continuous Pareto frontier over multiple rewards, enabling inference-time control of trade-offs (via a slider) without committing to a single weighted reward at training time.
problem_solved: Existing RL post-training methods collapse multiple objectives into a single scalar (early scalarization), forcing a fixed trade-off chosen during training and preventing users from adjusting competing goals (e.g., prompt adherence vs. source fidelity) at inference.
method: Post-train diffusion models with multiple reward signals so the model learns outcomes across conflicting objectives rather than a single scalar reward.
Condition the model on a continuous trade-off variable (the "slider") so sampling traces a learned Pareto frontier between objectives.
At inference, users set the slider to select any point on the frontier, obtaining continuous control over competing rewards without retraining.
impact: Allows practitioners to steer generative behavior in real time along meaningful trade-offs, reducing the need for multiple specialized models or repeated fine-tuning and improving alignment in multi-criteria tasks like image editing and content safety.
visual_elements: Pareto frontier plot with a movable slider showing positions corresponding to different trade-offs between two objectives.
Before/after example sequence (e.g., image edits) sampled at several slider values to illustrate changing trade-offs (fidelity vs. prompt adherence).
Pipeline diagram: pretrained diffusion model → Pareto post-training with multi-reward signals → slider-conditioned sampling at inference.
Metric chart/heatmap showing how objective scores vary continuously as the slider moves along the Pareto frontier.
paper_title: ParetoSlider: Diffusion Models Post-Training for Continuous Reward Control
paper_authors: Shelly Golan, Michael Finkelson, Ariel Bereslavsky, Yotam Nitzan, Or Patashnik
